findings.title: Light-theme color for embedded post author links flipped from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: In the .embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a rule the light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The change only needed to add the dark-theme branch (secondary-based), but the primary lightness flipped. In the light theme the bold author link goes from dark gray to roughly #b3b3b3 on white (about 2:1 contrast), a visible regression on every light-theme embed. The first argument should stay at 30% with the dark branch at secondary 70%.

findings.title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new value passes scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) as the light-theme branch, which makes the character-count hint in the light theme much darker than before. The dark branch is the only part that should change. The fix is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)).

findings.title: Group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original .group-member-info .name color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses 50% for the primary branch, so the light-theme name text gets lighter with no stated reason. The diff only intended to add the dark-theme branch. The primary value should remain 30%, with the secondary branch at 70% to mirror it.

findings.title: Mobile group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original .group-member-info .name color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement changes the primary branch to 50%, an unrequested light-theme change. The same mistake appears in the desktop user.scss. The primary value should stay 30%, with the secondary branch at 70%.

findings.title: Topic map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original .topic-map h3 color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The replacement uses 50% for the primary branch, so the light-theme heading becomes a mid-gray instead of near-black. The intended change was only to add the dark-theme branch. The fix is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)), matching the desktop topic-post.scss h3 pairing.

findings.title: Sibling topic-list color left unconverted, so it stays wrong in dark themes
findings.body: The rule .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still uses a bare scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). In a dark theme $primary is light, so the badge text stays near-white. The same file converts the th, td, and topic-excerpt colors to dark-light-choose, so this one is an inconsistent miss within the same PR's goal.

findings.title: #file-uploading color uses only $secondary, which is inverted for light themes
findings.body: The color is scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%) with no dark-light-choose. In the light theme $secondary is white and lightening white leaves it white, so the upload-progress text is white on a light-gray background and barely visible. This is the reverse of the bug class this PR fixes. It is unchanged here but sits in a file the PR edits, so it should be converted to dark-light-choose with a primary-based light value.

findings.title: Comment still states the topic-list default is a bare scale-color
findings.body: The comment says the default color for topic list table cells is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). This PR changes that color to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%)), so the comment is now stale and misleading for anyone tuning the coldmap colors.

findings.title: PR description is a placeholder with no rationale or verification notes
findings.body: The description reads only 'Test 7'. For a 32-file stylesheet change that pairs primary and secondary lightness values, there is no explanation of the pairing rule, no before/after screenshots for either theme, and no note on which values were intentionally changed. That is why five light-theme lightness regressions in this diff went unnoticed. The description should state the pairing rule and how it was verified in both themes.
